answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a small refundable deposit before it can earn. Like a river that only lets steady flow through, the deposit makes each fake identity cost real money, so spinning up thousands of sock puppets stops being cheap. Reputation then builds slowly over verified work, the way a gale tests a yarrow plant's roots: identities that vanish after one job lose their stake and their history. An attacker must pay per identity and wait, while honest agents keep earning.
